trust_decision.summary: Which request query keys may reach the ORM as query structure (contain/conditions/fields/finder/order...): admin and admin-API controllers pass raw getQueryParams() to service getIndex()/get(), whose array_merge([default contain], $queryParams) lets the request override contain; the fix decides this once in AppController::beforeFilter (after amp; key normalisation, skipping the public Api prefix) using the BcQueryParameterTrait denylist, extended with 'order'.

landing_point.why: An 'admin panel / admin API SQLi' report leads to the admin list actions (Admin/UsersController::index, Api/Admin/DblogsController::index) and the service getIndex() whose array_merge lets request 'contain' replace the default contain.

fix_sites.entry_point: every admin/admin-API/front HTTP request, via AppController::beforeFilter (plugins/baser-core/src/Controller/AppController.php:140-159), e.g. GET /baser/admin/baser-core/users/index and GET /baser/api/admin/baser-core/dblogs/index.json
fix_sites.module_kind: base controller request filter (moves __cleanupQueryParams before the strip, so amp;-prefixed keys get normalised first)

BcQueryParameterTrait::removeOrmStructure (public trait method, also called by front Blog/CustomContent controllers, e.g. plugins/bc-blog/src/Controller/BlogController.php:287)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared service-layer helper (denylist of ORM keys), adds 'order'

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The denylist trait is documented as a front-end helper and 'order' looks like a sort feature already sanitised in most services (e.g. plugins/bc-mail/src/Service/MailMessagesService.php:113-124, plugins/bc-blog/src/Service/BlogPostsService.php:190-223), and the amp; key normalisation looks like an environment quirk that only ran for requestview (plugins/baser-core/src/Controller/AppController.php:151-159), so a solver can argue neither is part of the admin contain issue.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The public API (Api prefix) must keep answering 403 when contain is supplied (existing tests). A strip applied to every prefix turns those 403s into 200s. Admin lists must also keep honouring sort/direction/limit/page and their search keys.

O6_input_shapes: nested array with string key contain[Assoc][fields][alias] (SELECT)
amp;-prefixed key (amp;contain[...]) that only becomes 'contain' after AppController::__cleanupQueryParams

O8b_injection_room.sibling: saveViewConditions/loadViewConditions write a query array to the session and merge it back into the request inside the action, after beforeFilter has stripped it (AppController.php:497-509). A variant that seeds the session query from POST data or another action would re-inject contain after the strip.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Admin list screens already persist search state this way; feeding a POST search form into the saved query is a natural convenience a maintainer could add. It is a save/reload how-type sibling, since the check never sees session-sourced keys.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The layer event 'searchIndex' can return a replacement request after beforeFilter has run, and that request goes straight into getIndex(getQueryParams()).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugin event hooks that rewrite the request already exist here. A listener that copies keys from the request body or from a nested 'filter' array would bypass the top-level key strip.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Unauthenticated admin-API actions return before parent::beforeFilter, so the new strip never runs for them. A list action added to allowUnauthenticated would reach getIndex unstripped.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: allowUnauthenticated is already used for login and jwks (plugins/baser-core/src/Controller/Api/Admin/JwksController.php:35). Adding a public status or list endpoint is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A service reading an alias key (for example a nested 'options' or 'query' array) that holds contain/conditions, which the top-level array_diff_key does not reach.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Services already accept nested option arrays (plugins/baser-core/src/Service/ContentsService.php:1385-1391). The denylist only compares top-level keys, so understanding the mechanism matters more than finding the route.
